This file documents the lei_entities resource at the shell, one section per command. Every command is a subcommand of =lei_entities=, and every section exports its own script into =projects/ores.shell/scripts/library/=. Loading a script runs that one command, so a failure names the command it came from.

* Commands

** =list=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: F9B0E360-A96F-58F9-A20A-52494D727926
:END:

Reads one page of the collection. Nothing addresses it but the caller's tenant, so it is the read that shows what exists.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
lei_entities list [--offset <n>] [--limit <n>] [--order <field>] [--desc]
#+end_example

It is addressed at =dq.v1.lei_entities.list=.

#+name: lei_entities-list
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle lei_entities-list.ores :exports none
lei_entities list --limit 1
#+end_src

** =get=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 7F6D6C26-1BD5-5465-8776-7119148DD322
:END:

Reads the one row its key addresses. A key states every identifying column, so a partial key is refused rather than answered with an arbitrary row.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
lei_entities get <lei>
#+end_example

It is addressed at =dq.v1.lei_entities.get=.

#+name: lei_entities-get
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle lei_entities-get.ores :exports none
lei_entities get __none__
#+end_src

** =get-many=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: FD63ECB4-B5DB-5781-B505-BAFDB6455EB3
:END:

Reads several rows in one request, one key group per row.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
lei_entities get-many <lei>
#+end_example

It is addressed at =dq.v1.lei_entities.get_many=.

#+name: lei_entities-get-many
